description: A reference type annotated with `?` (such as `string?`) that tells the compiler `null` is an expected value; the annotation exists only at compile time.
`T?` for a value type is `Nullable<T>`, a real runtime struct with `HasValue` and `Value`.
The `<Nullable>` project setting (or a `#nullable` directive) that decides whether annotations and warnings are on; new templates set it to `enable`.
The compiler's per-expression verdict, not-null or maybe-null, updated by assignments, null checks and control flow.
The postfix `!` that silences a nullability warning for one expression without adding any runtime check.
Attributes such as `[NotNullWhen(true)]` and `[MaybeNullWhen(false)]` that describe null contracts a plain `?` cannot express.
C# 14 syntax `a?.B = value` that performs the assignment only when `a` is not null and otherwise skips evaluating the right side.
A `System.Text.Json` option, available since .NET 9 and off by default, that throws when JSON supplies an explicit `null` for a non-nullable property.
